title: Building this blog: Flask, SQLite and vanilla JS
content: Flask serves the pages, SQLite stores the posts, and a small script.js fetches them from /api/posts. No frameworks, just the basics working together.

title: What is overfitting in machine learning?
content: A model that memorizes the training data performs badly on new data. Use a train/test split, keep the model simple, and gather more data to keep it honest.

title: Git in four commands
content: git add stages your changes, git commit saves a snapshot, git push uploads it, and git pull brings down changes from others. Commit small and often.

title: Why you should use parameterized queries
content: Never build SQL by joining strings with user input. Use placeholders like ? and pass the values separately so an attacker cannot inject their own SQL.

title: SQL basics: SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY
content: SELECT picks columns, WHERE filters rows and ORDER BY sorts the result. Add DESC to see the newest rows first, which is exactly how this blog lists its posts.

title: Sessions in Flask: remembering who logged in
content: Flask stores session data in a signed cookie. Set session["logged_in"] = True after a valid login, and check it at the top of any protected route.

title: Your first Flask route
content: Create an app with Flask(__name__), decorate a function with @app.route("/") and return a string or render_template. Run it and you have a working web server.

title: Four pillars of OOP in Python
content: Encapsulation hides internal state, inheritance reuses code, polymorphism lets different classes share an interface, and abstraction exposes only what the caller needs.

title: Python list comprehensions with real examples
content: A comprehension like [x * x for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0] builds a list in one readable line. If the logic gets long, switch back to a normal loop.

title: Fetch and async/await made simple
content: fetch returns a promise. Wrap it in an async function, await the response, check res.ok, then call res.json(). Add try/catch so network errors do not fail silently.

title: Reading input values with DOM events
content: Attach a submit listener to the form, call preventDefault, then read values from form.elements. The page stays put and you decide what happens next.

title: let, const and var: what actually changes
content: var is function-scoped and hoisted, while let and const are block-scoped. Default to const, switch to let only when the value must change, and skip var.

title: Flexbox vs Grid: when I use which
content: Flexbox is for one-dimensional layouts like navbars and button rows. Grid is for two dimensions, like a card gallery where rows and columns both matter.

title: The CSS box model in five minutes
content: Every element is a box: content, padding, border and margin. Add box-sizing: border-box and width finally includes padding and border, which saves a lot of layout headaches.

title: Semantic HTML: why div is not always the answer
content: Tags like header, nav, main, article and footer describe what the content is. Screen readers and search engines understand them, and your markup becomes easier to read.
